new_entities.name: Polarised endurance training distribution
aliases: mostly easy plus some very hard training distribution
new_entities.description: An endurance-training model with most work at low intensity, very little near threshold, and a smaller high-intensity component.

new_entities.name: VO2max
new_entities.description: The maximum rate of oxygen uptake during intense exercise, commonly used as a marker of aerobic fitness.

edges.effect_quant: The newest individual-participant network meta-analysis found no overall VO2max difference between polarised and pyramidal intensity distributions (SMD -0.06, p = 0.68), though competitive athletes may respond better to polarised training than recreational athletes. Earlier randomized-trial evidence suggested polarised training may outperform threshold-focused models for endurance performance, but direct VO2max superiority is much less consistent than the broader performance narrative.
edges.population: recreational and competitive endurance-trained athletes using structured intensity-distribution models
edges.mechanism: Polarised training may balance high aerobic volume with enough very hard work to stimulate central and peripheral adaptation while avoiding excessive threshold fatigue, but the exact aerobic-capacity response depends on athlete level and what comparator model is used.
edges.summary: This is a good example of a coaching idea that is stronger for performance than for one single biomarker. Polarised training can be an excellent endurance model, but the current VO2max-specific literature is mixed rather than decisively superior across all athletes.
edges.caveats: Competitive athletes may benefit more than recreational ones. Also, not every study uses the same zone definitions or comparator model, which makes clean one-line conclusions about VO2max difficult.

evidence.notes: Which Training Intensity Distribution Intervention will Produce the Greatest Improvements in Maximal Oxygen Uptake and Time-Trial Performance in Endurance Athletes? A Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis of Individual Participant Data.

evidence.citation: RosenblatMA et al 2019 J Strength Cond Res
evidence.notes: Polarized vs. Threshold Training Intensity Distribution on Endurance Sport Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
